agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

hwatch
======

A modern alternative to the watch command. hwatch records command execution results, keeps a history, and can show diffs between runs.

Features
--------
- Records command outputs over time and keeps a history of results.
- Shows differences between executions and supports multiple diff modes.
- Can output results as JSON logs.
- Customizable keybindings and display options.
- Supports ANSI color codes and scrollable output.

Usage
-----
Run hwatch followed by the command you want to monitor. Example:

    hwatch [OPTIONS] [command]...

Common options (user-facing):
- -b, --batch       : Output execution results to stdout instead of the UI.
- -c, --color       : Interpret ANSI color and style sequences in command output.
- -n, --interval    : Seconds to wait between updates (default: 2).
- -l, --logfile     : Write execution history as a JSON log file.
- -h, --help        : Print help.

Configuration
-------------
You can set default options using an environment variable (for example, HWATCH) if you want to always enable certain flags.

Examples
--------
Run a command every 3 seconds:

    hwatch -n 3 command...

Log command outputs to a JSON file:

    hwatch -n 3 -l hwatch_log.json command...

Additional help
---------------
See the manual pages in the man/ directory (if present) or run `hwatch --help` for a full list of options and keybindings.

hwatch
======

A modern alternative to the watch command. hwatch records command execution results, keeps a history, and can show diffs between runs.

Features
--------
- Records command outputs over time and keeps a history of results.
- Shows differences between executions and supports multiple diff modes.
- Can output results as JSON logs.
- Customizable keybindings and display options.
- Supports ANSI color codes and scrollable output.

Usage
-----
Run hwatch followed by the command you want to monitor. Example:

    hwatch [OPTIONS] [command]...

Common options (user-facing):
- -b, --batch       : Output execution results to stdout instead of the UI.
- -c, --color       : Interpret ANSI color and style sequences in command output.
- -n, --interval    : Seconds to wait between updates (default: 2).
- -l, --logfile     : Write execution history as a JSON log file.
- -h, --help        : Print help.

Configuration
-------------
You can set default options using an environment variable (for example, HWATCH) if you want to always enable certain flags.

Examples
--------
Run a command every 3 seconds:

    hwatch -n 3 command...

Log command outputs to a JSON file:

    hwatch -n 3 -l hwatch_log.json command...

Additional help
---------------
See the manual pages in the man/ directory (if present) or run `hwatch --help` for a full list of options and keybindings.

% hwatch(1) Version 0.3.16 | A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

NAME
====

**hwatch** - A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

SYNOPSIS
========

| **hwatch** \[*options*] *command*

DESCRIPTION
===========

**hwatch** is like *watch* command, repeatedly executes a *command* and displays its output.
However, the output results can be scrolled and displayed.
In addition, the difference of the execution result is recorded with the time stamp, and it can be checked later.
When checking, it is also possible to display the diff with the previous difference together.

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use std::io::{self, Write};

fn build_command() -> Command {
    Command::new("hwatch")
        .version("0.3.19")
        .about("A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.")
        .disable_help_flag(true)
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .arg(Arg::new("batch").short('b').long("batch").help("output execution results to stdout").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("beep").short('B').long("beep").help("beep if command has a change result").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("border").long("border").help("Surround each pane with a border frame").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("with-scrollbar").long("with-scrollbar").help("When the border option is enabled, display scrollbar on the right side of watch pane.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("mouse").long("mouse").help("enable mouse wheel support. With this option, copying text with your terminal may be harder. Try holding the Shift key.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("color").short('c').long("color").help("interpret ANSI color and style sequences").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("reverse").short('r').long("reverse").help("display text upside down.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("compress").short('C').long("compress").help("Compress data in memory. Note: If the output of the command is small, you may not get the desired effect.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-title").short('t').long("no-title").help("hide the UI on start. Use `t` to toggle it.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("enable-summary-char").long("enable-summary-char").help("collect character-level diff count in summary.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("line-number").short('N').long("line-number").help("show line number").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-help-banner").long("no-help-banner").help("hide the \"Display help with h key\" message").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("no-summary").long("no-summary").help("disable the calculation for summary that is running behind the scenes, and disable the summary function in the first place.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("exec").short('x').long("exec").help("Run the command directly, not through the shell. Much like the `-x` option of the watch command.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("diff-output-only").short('O').long("diff-output-only").help("Display only the lines with differences during `line` diff and `word` diff.").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("aftercommand").short('A').long("aftercommand").value_name("after_command").help("Executes the specified command if the output changes. Information about changes is stored in json format in environment variable ${HWATCH_DATA}.").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("logfile").short('l').long("logfile").value_name("logfile").help("logging file. if a log file is already used, its contents will be read and executed.").num_args(0..=1).action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("shell").short('s').long("shell").value_name("shell_command").help("shell to use at runtime. can also insert the command to the location specified by {COMMAND}.").default_value("sh -c").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("interval").short('n').long("interval").value_name("interval").help("seconds to wait between updates").default_value("2").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(f64)).action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("precise").long("precise").help("Attempt to run as close to the interval as possible, regardless of how long the command takes to run").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("limit").short('L').long("limit").value_name("limit").help("Set the number of history records to keep. only work in watch mode. Set `0` for unlimited recording. (default: 5000)").default_value("5000").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u64)))
        .arg(Arg::new("tab-size").long("tab-size").value_name("tab_size").help("Specifying tab display size").default_value("4").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u64)).action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("differences").short('d').long("differences").value_name("differences").help("highlight changes between updates").num_args(0..=1).value_parser(["none","watch","line","word"]).default_missing_value("watch").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("output").short('o').long("output").value_name("output").help("Select command output.").num_args(0..=1).value_parser(["output","stdout","stderr"]).default_value("output").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("keymap").short('K').long("keymap").value_name("keymap").help("Add keymap").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("help").short('h').long("help").help("Print help").action(ArgAction::Help))
        .arg(Arg::new("version").short('V').long("version").help("Print version").action(ArgAction::Version))
        .arg(Arg::new("command").num_args(0..).trailing_var_arg(true).allow_hyphen_values(true))
}

fn main() {
    // HWATCH env handling: split by whitespace, prepend
    let hwatch_extra: Vec<String> = std::env::var("HWATCH").map(|s| s.split_whitespace().map(|x| x.to_string()).collect()).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().collect();
    // args[0] is program name, insert hwatch_extra after it
    let prog = args.remove(0);
    let mut full_args = vec![prog];
    full_args.extend(hwatch_extra);
    full_args.extend(args);
    let cmd = build_command();
    // need to handle bin name for Usage: clap uses argv0 automatically if we pass full_args
    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(full_args);
    match matches {
        Ok(m) => {
            // handle normal
            println!("parsed ok batch={} command={:?}", m.get_flag("batch"), m.get_many::<String>("command").map(|v| v.collect::<Vec<_>>()));
        },
        Err(e) => {
            // clap error: print to stderr and exit with code
            e.print().unwrap();
            std::process::exit(e.exit_code());
        }
    }
}

    if env:
        e.update(env)
    full = ["timeout", str(timeout), cmd] + args
    p = subprocess.run(full, capture_output=True, text=True, env=e)
    def norm(s):
        s = re.sub(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d{3}', 'TS', s)
        s = re.sub(r"thread '(.*?)' \(\d+\)", r"thread '\1' (PID)", s)
        # normalize bin name in Usage? For now, replace hwatch/executable with BIN
        s = s.replace('Usage: hwatch', 'Usage: BIN').replace('Usage: executable', 'Usage: BIN')
        return s
    return norm(p.stdout), norm(p.stderr), p.returncode

        if m:
            key=m.group(1)
            desc_line=help_lines[i+1]
            if 'key :' not in desc_line:  # desc line, not next key
                desc=desc_line.replace('│','').strip()
                if key not in seen and '─' not in desc and '┌' not in desc and desc:
                    pairs.append((key,desc))
                    seen.add(key)
    # scroll by 2 to keep alignment (one entry = 2 lines)
    pane.send_keys('Down')
    time.sleep(0.05)

    time.sleep(0.05)

fn validate_keymap(km: &str) -> bool {
    if km.matches('=').count() != 1 { return false; }
    let parts: Vec<&str> = km.splitn(2, '=').collect();
    if parts.len() != 2 { return false; }
    let key = parts[0].trim();
    let action = parts[1].trim();
    if key.is_empty() || action.is_empty() { return false; }
    if key.chars().any(|c| c.is_whitespace()) { return false; }
    if action.chars().any(|c| c.is_whitespace()) { return false; }
    if !validate_key(key) { return false; }
    if !validate_action(action) { return false; }
    true
}
fn validate_key(key: &str) -> bool {
    if key.chars().count() == 1 {
        let ch = key.chars().next().unwrap();
        let code = ch as u32;
        if code < 33 || code > 126 { return false; }
        if ch == '-' || ch == ':' || ch == '=' || ch == '[' || ch == '\\' { return false; }
        return true;
</output>
